competency_fulfillment.rationale: Every stem uses the competency's own verb and noun ('Estimate the quotient', 'Estimate: ___ ≈ ___'), and hand-checking the rounding-then-dividing method against each stem confirms the answers are genuine estimates, not disguised exact division: 150 ÷ 16 rounds the 3-digit dividend to 200 (half-up), giving floor(200/16)=12, which is clearly not the exact quotient 9 that 150 ÷ 16 actually yields.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All seven sampled dividends (120, 320, 505, 100, 150, 450, 170) are 3-digit numbers and every divisor (76, 18, 60, 22, 16, 54, 40) is 2-digit, so the competency's own '2- to 3-digit divided by 1- to 2-digit' range is only half-exercised here — no sample in this packet shows a 2-digit dividend or a single-digit divisor being estimated.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Sentence forms stay short and grade-appropriate ('Estimate the quotient: 320 ÷ 18', 'Grace says: 170 ÷ 40 ≈ 160. Is Grace correct?'), the vocabulary (quotient, estimate) matches the exact MATATAG term set for this competency, and the reasoning load — round then divide — is a single well-scaffolded step suited to Grade 3 Quarter 4.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Four distinct representational formats appear across the seven seeds — direct MCQ estimate (seed 42), cloze fill-in (seed 44), true/false statement check (seed 50), and error-detection with a named student, Grace (seed 55) — giving real format variety even though none frames the task as a narrative word problem, which the competency's wording does not itself require.

competency_alignment.rationale: The sampled items vary difficulty through rounding-boundary tricks like 150 (exactly halfway between 100 and 200, forcing a round-half-up decision before dividing by 16), which does build the estimation skill, but since no 2-digit-dividend case appears, the progression never demonstrates scaffolding from the competency's easier tier up to its 3-digit tier.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: Dividends span 100–505 and divisors span 16–76, both comfortably inside the competency's stated 3-digit-by-2-digit ceiling with no overflow into 4-digit territory, and re-deriving floor(round(dividend)/divisor) by hand for all seven seeds — including the 200/16=12 and 500/60=8 cases — matches every recorded correct_answer exactly.
